objects.description: A proxy class that wraps an AnchoredSetVariable and translates the resulting VariableValue entries to appear under a different variable name (m_name). After delegating resolution to the underlying AnchoredSetVariable (m_fount), it replaces each returned VariableValue with a newly constructed one using the proxy's name and copies origin metadata, then deletes the original. Provides resolve methods for full set, with key exclusions, by key, and by regular expression, plus a helper to fetch the first value. Ownership note: resolve methods allocate new VariableValue objects and transfer them to the caller via the output vector; the caller is responsible for deleting them (as shown in resolveFirst).
Case-insensitive equality functor for std::string, comparing length and then character-by-character using tolower. Useful as the key equality predicate in unordered containers.
Case-insensitive hash functor for std::string that sums lowercase character codes. Intended to pair with MyEqual in unordered containers. Hash quality is low as noted in comment.

A case-insensitive multimap of string keys to VariableValue* with additional helper methods to set, unset, and resolve values by key or regular expression. Inherits from std::unordered_multimap<std::string, VariableValue*, MyHash, MyEqual>. Holds a Transaction context pointer and the variable set name.
Forward declaration of the modsecurity::Transaction class. Only a declaration is present in this header; the class is defined elsewhere. Details of its interface and lifecycle are unknown here.

A C++ helper class representing an "anchored" variable within a ModSecurity Transaction. It stores a variable name, computed value, and offset, and offers methods to set/unset and evaluate the variable, returning either a list-oriented evaluation into VariableValue pointers, a raw string pointer, or the first resolved value as a unique_ptr. Copy and assignment are disabled; lifetime is independent but it holds a raw pointer to the owning Transaction. Internals include a VariableValue member used during evaluation.

Forward-declared interface/class representing an audit log writer implementation used by AuditLog. Only a forward declaration is present in this header; no members are defined here. Details such as constructors, methods, and lifetime management are unknown from this file.

Main ModSecurity audit logging controller. Provides configuration (paths, permissions, format, parts), lifecycle (init/close), relevance filtering, and save/merge operations. Owns a writer implementation pointer and exposes enums defining log type, status, format, and bitmask parts. Copy is disabled; destructor is virtual. Construction is via default constructor; initialization expected through init().
Enumeration defining how audit logs are written: not set, serial (single log stream), parallel (per-transaction entries), or HTTPS (remote). Used to configure AuditLog behavior via setType().
Enumeration controlling whether audit logging is on, off, relevant-only, or not set. Used by setStatus() and relevance checks.
Enumeration selecting audit log output format: JSON or native (legacy), or not set.

Abstract base class representing a ModSecurity rule. Stores source file/line metadata and evaluation phase. Requires derived classes to implement evaluate() methods. Not copyable. Lifetime managed by user; no ownership semantics specified here.

Concrete Rule subtype that represents a SecMarker (rule marker) used for flow control within rule sets. It stores the marker name and, when evaluated, checks the transaction's current marker and removes it if it matches. Copying is disabled. Construction requires a marker name plus source file and line metadata. Other lifecycle details (ownership/destruction) follow Rule; no special destruction beyond default is needed.

Concrete rule class that always exists independent of conditions and inherits behavior from RuleWithActions. It exposes the evaluate method, which takes a Transaction and a RuleMessage reference. The constructor set is inherited from RuleWithActions via a using-declaration. Details of evaluation semantics are not provided in this header.

C++ rule class that extends modsecurity::Rule to attach and manage actions and transformations. It encapsulates rule evaluation, execution of actions (including disruptive/blocking), transformation pipelines, logging, and chaining of rules. Instances may be linked as chained parent/child. Construction requires action and transformation lists plus source location. Destruction is virtual and follows Rule’s interface. Detailed behavior of referenced types (Actions, Transformations, Transaction, RuleMessage, actions::Action, etc.) is defined elsewhere.

C++ rule class that couples a RuleWithActions with a specific operator and a set of variables to evaluate. It owns no resources by value; instead it holds non-owning pointers to a variables set and an operator. It provides evaluation, variable exception handling, and operator execution helpers. Construction requires an operator, variables set, actions list, transformations, and source location. Destruction is virtual and overridden; ownership semantics of passed-in pointers are not defined here and likely managed elsewhere in the engine.

Container class in namespace modsecurity that owns and manages a sequence of Rule objects. Provides insertion with optional duplicate-ID checks (against RuleWithOperator::m_ruleId), append/merge from another Rules, iteration via size()/operator[]/at(), and a dump() helper for debugging. Ownership is via std::shared_ptr stored in m_rules.

Represents a loggable message produced by evaluation of a ModSecurity rule. Holds references to the originating RuleWithActions and Transaction, message text, match details, severity, tags, and audit/logging flags. Provides instance and static helpers to format log strings, error log tails, and details. Copy construction is allowed; assignment is disabled. The inner enum LogMessageInfo defines bit flags that affect logging output.
Bit-flag enum inside RuleMessage controlling which parts of a log entry are included. ErrorLogTailLogMessageInfo adds the error log tail; ClientLogMessageInfo formats for client logs.

A concrete rules container and manager in the modsecurity namespace. It derives from RulesSetProperties and encapsulates rule loading (from URI, remote, file, or strings), merging, evaluation across phases, debugging, and cleanup helpers. It owns a RulesSetPhases member for phase-specific organization and conditionally tracks a secmarker skip counter when logging is enabled. Constructors allow default creation with a new DebugLog or using a provided DebugLog. Destruction semantics are not detailed here; refer to owning base or implementation for resource management.

C++ class that organizes and manages ModSecurity Rules instances by execution phase. It stores an array of eight Rules containers (likely corresponding to the engine phases) and provides methods to insert a single Rule into the appropriate phase, append rules from another RulesSetPhases, dump internal state, and access phase-specific Rules via operator[]/at(). Exact behavior of phases and Rule/Rules come from other headers.

Configuration container holding a set of strings, with flags indicating set/clear behavior for merging.

Holds configuration for Unicode code page mapping: whether set, selected code page, and a shared UnicodeMapHolder. Provides static loadConfig and merge.

Aggregates ModSecurity rule-set configurable properties, defaults, and merge logic. Owns logging components, numeric/string/set configs, default actions per phase, and enums describing engine behavior. Provides constructors, destructor, and a static mergeProperties routine.
Tri-state boolean for configuration fields: true, false, or not set.
Four-state selector controlling XML parsing into arguments: true, false, only args, or not set.
Controls rule evaluation mode: disabled, enabled (enforce), detection-only, or not set.
Action to take when body exceeds limits: process partial, reject, or not set.
Behavior when fetching remote rules fails: abort, warn, or not set.

C++ class that aggregates and applies rule-exception logic for ModSecurity. It supports loading and merging exception specifications, removing rules by message or tag, and updating rule targets or actions by message, tag, or ID. It maintains internal collections for ranges and explicit rule numbers, as well as multimaps for variable and action updates keyed by tag, message, or rule ID. Construction/destruction are standard C++ (constructor/destructor provided). Ownership: uses shared_ptr to refer to variables/actions and stores lists/multimaps internally. Specific parsing/semantics are defined in the implementation; details not present in this header.

Helper class that bundles all anchored variables exposed on a Transaction, pre-initializing AnchoredVariable and AnchoredSetVariable members bound to a Transaction. Used as a base class of Transaction.
Utility class that manages SecMarker state within a transaction, tracking whether execution is inside a named marker and providing accessors to set, clear, and query the current marker.

Core ModSecurity transaction object. Manages request/response processing, variables, body processors, collections, audit/logging, and interventions for a single HTTP transaction. Non-copyable; constructed with a ModSecurity and RulesSet context.
Enumeration inside Transaction describing request body types supported by ModSecurity for specialized processing.

C++ class representing the origin (offset and length) of a variable value, likely within some input buffer. Provides two constructors (default sets both to 0; parameterized sets both values) and a toText() helper that serializes as "v<offset>,<length>". Members m_length and m_offset are public size_t fields. No ownership semantics or special construction APIs are defined in this header.

C++ class representing a ModSecurity variable instance. It stores the collection name, key, combined key (collection:key), value, and a list of VariableOrigin entries indicating where the value came from. Copy-construction is explicitly deleted; it supports construction from key/value pointers, collection+key+value pointers, and a cloning-style constructor from another VariableValue pointer that duplicates origins. Used to read and mutate a variable's value and to record provenance of that value.

Abstract base class representing a key/value collection used by ModSecurity to store and query variables, with compartmentalized namespacing via '::'. It defines pure-virtual CRUD, expiry, and resolution interfaces that derived classes must implement, plus helper overloads that compose compartmented keys. Holds a name identifier in m_name. Construction requires a collection name; destruction is virtual. No ownership relationships are defined in this header.

C++ class representing a bundle of ModSecurity persistent collections (global, ip, session, user, resource) along with their corresponding key strings. Provides a constructor accepting pointers to existing Collection instances and a destructor. Copy and assignment are disabled. Holds raw pointers to underlying Collection objects and key strings for each collection. Details about lifecycle and ownership semantics are not documented here; based on the header, this class likely does not own the passed-in Collection instances and merely references them.

Concrete base class for ModSecurity rule actions. It parses an action string into a name and optional payload and tracks when the action should execute via the nested Kind enum. Provides virtual hooks to initialize and evaluate an action against a Transaction/RuleWithActions, and flags for disruptive or temporary actions. Copy/move is disabled; instances manage an optional shared action name and parser payload.
Strongly-typed enum nested in Action that classifies when an action executes: at configuration load, before operator execution, or only if the operator matched.

functions.name: modsecurity::AnchoredSetVariableTranslationProxy::resolve
functions.description: Resolves all values from the underlying AnchoredSetVariable and translates each entry to use this proxy’s variable name. The vector l is modified in place: entries are replaced with newly allocated VariableValue objects; the old entries are deleted inside this function.
requirements: Parameter l must be a valid, non-null pointer to a std::vector of pointers to const modsecurity::VariableValue.
This function replaces and deletes every entry currently in l, not just newly-added ones; callers should pass an empty vector unless they intend for existing entries to be re-keyed and destroyed.
After the call, l contains heap-allocated VariableValue pointers owned by the caller; the caller must delete each element after use to avoid memory leaks.
Function may append or fill results depending on the underlying fount; exact semantics of accumulation are not documented.
Not thread-safe by specification; concurrency expectations are unknown.

functions.name: modsecurity::AnchoredSetVariableTranslationProxy::resolve

Parameter ke must be a valid modsecurity::variables::KeyExclusions instance; its exact required state is not specified.
All entries currently in l will be replaced and deleted; callers should generally pass an empty vector unless they intend existing entries to be re-keyed and destroyed.
After the call, the caller owns and must delete every VariableValue pointer in l when done.

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List, Tuple

# Target: fuzzer-generated file data
# The fuzzer stubs pass FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() to APIs that expect paths to files.
# Our generate() should return initial file contents that make those APIs behave meaningfully.
# We craft a small virtual filesystem payload that can be written as the fuzz file content.
# Desirable coverage:
# - Looks like rules text (for RulesSet loaders)
# - Looks like an auditlog parts string (for setParts)
# - Looks like JSON or text (for DebugLog messages)
# - Looks like HTTP body (for requestBodyFromFile)
# We multiplex several plausible sections separated by clear markers so any reader can parse some.

MAX_SIZE = 4096

HTTP_BODIES = [
    # Simple URL-encoded form
    b"name=alice&role=admin&flag=1",
    # JSON
    b"{\n  \"user\": \"bob\",\n  \"id\": 123,\n  \"tags\": [\"x\", \"y\"]\n}",
    # Multipart-like (very small)
    b"--AaB03x\r\nContent-Disposition: form-data; name=field1\r\n\r\nvalue1\r\n--AaB03x--\r\n",
]

RULE_SNIPPETS = [
    # Minimalistic CRS-like style lines that loaders might accept
    b"SecRuleEngine On\n",
    b"SecAction id:1001,phase:1,pass,log,msg:'hello'\n",
    b"SecMarker END_TEST\n",
]

PARTS_STRINGS = [
    b"ABCFHZ",
    b"-C+I",
    b"ABCEFKZ",
]

DEBUG_LINES = [
    b"[debug] id=100 uri=/index msg=ok\n",
    b"test message for debug log path handling\n",
]

def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, items: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    return rng.choice(items)

def _rand_printable(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(string.printable.rstrip()) for _ in range(n))
    return s.encode('utf-8', 'ignore')

def build_composite_file(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    chunks: List[bytes] = []

    # Optional shebang-like path hint (some parsers ignore, some accept comments)
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        chunks.append(b"# path: /tmp/audit/logs/test.log\n")

    # Insert some rule snippets
    count_rules = rng.randint(1, 4)
    for _ in range(count_rules):
        chunks.append(_rand_choice(rng, RULE_SNIPPETS))

    # Add an audit log parts line possibly consumed by setParts
    if rng.random() < 0.9:
        chunks.append(b"# parts:\n")
        chunks.append(_rand_choice(rng, PARTS_STRINGS) + b"\n")

    # Add debug-style log lines
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        chunks.append(b"# debug:\n")
        chunks.append(_rand_choice(rng, DEBUG_LINES))

    # Separator
    chunks.append(b"\n-----BEGIN-BODY-----\n")

    # HTTP-like body
    chunks.append(_rand_choice(rng, HTTP_BODIES))

    # Maybe append some extra printable noise to exercise parsers safely
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        chunks.append(b"\n# extra:\n")
        chunks.append(_rand_printable(rng, rng.randint(16, 64)) + b"\n")

    # Ensure trailing newline
    chunks.append(b"\n")

    data = b"".join(chunks)
    if len(data) > MAX_SIZE:
        data = data[:MAX_SIZE]
    return data


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    return build_composite_file(rng)
